quote.text: I have two cars and lose track of which needs what

promise.text: How to keep track of maintenance on two cars

art.why: the carousel's topic: the moment and its guide name "car"

lines.text: Which car needs the oil change?
Keep a separate record for each car, label them by plate or name, and check both together once a month.

body.text: A plate is the safest, or a name that can't be mistaken, like the work van.
Put the year and make beside it, so a stranger could tell them apart.

head.text: Start one page, tab or notebook section per car, with the same columns on each: date, odometer, what was done, who did it.
Write each car's intervals on its own page, from its own manual.
Log the job on the day, and start the line with the car's label.

body.text: If you're at the shop with both keys, write it down before you leave the lot.

head.text: Once a month, read both odometers on the same day and check each page.

body.text: Pick a date you'll remember, such as the first Sunday.

line.text: Both sit in the same ranked list, most urgent first, each item saying which vehicle it belongs to.
